title: Forensic: reconcile audit ingestion gap after HSM rewrap and SSO token churn
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a scheduled HSM key rewrap on 2026-02-28 we observed a delayed and partial ingestion of audit events for a subset of customer shards which produced an 8-hour visibility gap in the centralized audit sink. Simultaneously, a burst of IdP (SSO) token rotations triggered short-lived auth failures in the agent that writes to the audit buffer. The combination revealed a fragile path in the rewrap + ingestion flow that allowed events to be dropped rather than durably queued and replayed.
timeline: 2026-02-28T01:20Z - Scheduled HSM rewrap started. 2026-02-28T01:35Z - First agent leader election restarted rewrap workers for shard group B. 2026-02-28T02:05Z - IdP rolled tokens in region-us-east causing ~6% auth error rate on audit forwarders. 2026-02-28T03:00Z - Central audit sink metrics show rising IngestLag for shards B and D. 2026-02-28T09:15Z - Reconciliation job discovered missing sequences and replayed buffered events for some customers (partial recovery). 2026-02-28T11:20Z - Full reconciliation completed for 92% of affected tenants; remaining gap persisted until manual export applied.
impact: Audit logs for ~14% of production tenants in us-east had incomplete trails for the period 2026-02-28T01:30Z to 2026-02-28T09:15Z. This affected compliance reporting, internal incident triage, and one regulated customer required an immediate SLA exemption and forensic export. No customer data was exfiltrated; integrity and confidentiality were maintained.
root_cause: Three contributing factors: (1) The rewrap coordinator did not atomically mark re-encryption progress for all shards before rotating active leader, leaving a tiny window where events were written under the old envelope key but not accepted by the sink verifier. (2) Audit forwarders lacked a durable disk-backed queue and dropped events on transient auth failures instead of retrying with exponential backoff + fallback. (3) IdP token churn coincided with rewrap, increasing transient auth errors beyond the current retry budget.
short_term_mitigation: - Re-enabled emergency backfill run for all affected shards and produced per-tenant manifests for compliance reports (completed 2026-03-02). - Increased forwarder retry window and added a local on-disk buffer to prevent drops during transient auth failures (hotfix deployed 2026-03-04). - Coordinated with IdP to stagger token rotations for future maintenance windows (agreement in engineering-ops channel).
long_term_actions: 1) Make audit forwarders durable: implement 24-hour local write-ahead queue with checksum and sequence tracking; owner: Priya Rao; due: 2026-04-10
2) Rewrap coordinator transactional mark: change leader handoff to commit rewrap state via consensus round before key rotation; owner: Mateo Garcia; due: 2026-04-03
3) Automated reconciliation: build a background verifier that compares source sequences to sink sequences and auto-replays gaps; owner: Li Wei; due: 2026-04-17
4) Alerting & SLOs: add audit-ingest-lag SLO (target < 5m) and an incident alert pathway for >1h lag with pager duty routing; owner: Emma Johnson; due: 2026-03-24
5) Runbook updates: add a pre-rewrap checklist that includes IdP maintenance window coordination and forwarder health checks; owner: Security Ops; due: 2026-03-15
6) Compliance package: create a tenant-export tooling template for rapid forensic exports and a customer comms playbook; owner: Customer Success + Legal; due: 2026-03-31
acceptance_criteria: - No dropped audit events observed in 3 staged rewrap drills (internal) across 3 regions. - Local forwarders can buffer 24 hours and resume without loss after IdP token rotation. - The verifier auto-replays at least 99.9% of detected gaps in a synthetic test harness.
risks: Implementing durable on-disk queues increases disk usage on forwarders and adds complexity to upgrade/rollback. Consensus change in rewrap coordinator risks longer maintenance windows if not properly tested. Coordination with IdP requires cross-org scheduling discipline.
